day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight AC lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Use transit (747 bus or STM metro) from the airport to your Old Montreal accommodation to save on transport costs (~$11 CAD vs $50+ taxi).
day_by_day.afternoon: After checking in, take a self-guided walk through Old Montreal (Vieux-Montréal). Explore Place Jacques-Cartier, stroll along the cobblestone streets of Rue Saint-Paul, and admire the Notre-Dame Basilica exterior for free. Get oriented with your neighbourhood and pick up a free city map from the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Old Montreal Culinary Walking Tour — Join an early evening guided culinary walk through Vieux-Montréal, stopping at historic bistros, bakeries, and local food stalls. This is a perfect low-key introduction to Montreal's food scene right from your doorstep. Book the latest available time slot to align with your afternoon arrival.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable bite near the airport or pick up a bagel and coffee from a depanneur (corner store) near your hotel on arrival (~$5–8 CAD)
meals.dinner: Included as tastings during the Old Montreal Culinary Walking Tour; supplement with a classic poutine from La Banquise's Old Montreal satellite or a local chip truck (~$12–15 CAD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you'll be tired from travel. Buy a 3-day STM transit pass (~$21 CAD) upon arrival to save money on all metro and bus rides throughout the trip. Check if your hotel offers free luggage storage if check-in isn't ready.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour — Head north by metro (Jean-Talon station, Orange Line) to explore one of North America's largest open-air markets. Sample Quebec cheeses, fresh maple products, seasonal fruits, and artisan breads. Arrive early (9:00–10:00) for the best atmosphere and freshest produce. Budget ~$15–20 CAD for tastings and small purchases.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood on foot. Browse the colourful murals along Rue Rachel and Rue Saint-Denis, visit Parc La Fontaine (free), and people-watch at one of the city's most beloved green spaces. Rent a BIXI bike (~$7 CAD for a 24-hr pass) to cover more ground affordably.
day_by_day.evening: St-Laurent Boulevard Street Food & Nightlife Crawl — Walk the iconic 'Main' (Boulevard Saint-Laurent) from Avenue des Pins southward, sampling diverse street food including legendary smoked meat sandwiches, shawarma, and Portuguese chicken. The warm July evening makes this outdoor crawl especially vibrant.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastry and café au lait from a boulangerie near your hotel (~$6–9 CAD)
meals.lunch: Eat at Jean-Talon Market itself — grab a fresh baguette, local cheese, and seasonal fruit for a picnic-style market lunch (~$10–14 CAD)
meals.dinner: St-Laurent Street Food Crawl — budget $20–25 CAD for multiple small bites: smoked meat sandwich at Schwartz's Deli (~$12), plus street snacks along the crawl

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is busiest on weekends but Thursday mornings are still lively and less crowded. Bring a small reusable bag for any market purchases. The BIXI bike network connects Plateau and Saint-Laurent easily.

day_by_day.morning: Climb Mont Royal for free — Take the metro to Mont-Royal station and hike up to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for a panoramic view of the city skyline. This iconic free activity is a Montreal must-do. Pack snacks from a local depanneur to enjoy at the summit (~$5 CAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience — Check the festival schedule for afternoon programming. Montreal en Lumière (or a July equivalent summer festival) often features free outdoor stages, culinary pop-ups, and cultural performances in the downtown core. Explore the festival grounds, enjoy free live music, and sample affordable festival food offerings.
day_by_day.evening: Continue at the Montreal en Lumière Festival for evening performances and gastronomy events. Many outdoor concerts and light installations are free. Splurge slightly on a festival food experience or cooking demonstration if budget allows (~$15–25 CAD for a ticketed tasting event).

meals.breakfast: Bagel with cream cheese from a St-Viateur or Fairmount-style bagel shop near the Plateau (~$4–6 CAD) — Montreal bagels are a must-try local staple
meals.lunch: Picnic on Mont Royal with market snacks and a sandwich from a nearby dépanneur or boulangerie (~$8–12 CAD)
meals.dinner: Festival food stalls at Montreal en Lumière — budget $18–25 CAD for a mix of local bites such as tourtière, maple-glazed dishes, and artisan cheeses

day_by_day.notes: Verify the exact festival dates and free vs. ticketed events on the official Montreal en Lumière website before the trip. July often features the Montreal Jazz Festival and other overlapping events — check for free outdoor stages running concurrently for extra entertainment at no cost.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Mile End neighbourhood — Walk or bike to this trendy, multicultural district known for its street art, independent cafés, and local character. Visit the famous Fairmount Bagel bakery (open 24/7) for a fresh-from-the-oven Montreal bagel (~$2 CAD each). Browse the colourful murals along Avenue Laurier and Rue Bernard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Marché Atwater (Atwater Market) in the Saint-Henri neighbourhood — a smaller but equally charming covered market with local vendors selling Quebec produce, charcuterie, and artisan goods. Stroll along the nearby Lachine Canal (free) and enjoy the warm summer weather along the waterfront bike path.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening back in Old Montreal — Return to your home base for a relaxed farewell dinner. Explore Rue Saint-Paul for affordable bistro options, or pick up supplies from a local grocery or dépanneur for a budget-friendly picnic along the Old Port waterfront. Watch the sunset over the St. Lawrence River at no cost.

meals.breakfast: Fresh Montreal bagels from Fairmount Bagel with butter or cream cheese (~$5–8 CAD)
meals.lunch: Atwater Market picnic — pick up local charcuterie, cheese, bread, and seasonal fruit for a self-assembled feast along the Lachine Canal (~$12–16 CAD)
meals.dinner: Old Montreal farewell meal — opt for a BYOB (apportez votre vin) restaurant on Rue Saint-Paul for significant savings; a two-course meal typically runs $20–28 CAD per person without the markup of a liquor licence

day_by_day.notes: Saturday at both markets is lively and festive — arrive at Atwater by 11:00 before crowds peak. BYOB restaurants are a uniquely Montreal tradition that dramatically cuts dining costs; pick up a bottle of wine at the SAQ or a dépanneur beforehand. Leave time to pack and confirm any checkout or late luggage storage arrangements with your hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Montreal-Trudeau Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Travel from airport to Old Montreal hotel (~30 min by taxi or ~45 min by 747 express bus). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighbourhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Culinary Walking Tour: After settling in, join an afternoon guided walk through the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal. Discover historic bistros, artisan bakeries, and local fromageries while learning about Quebec's culinary heritage. The tour departs steps from most Old Montreal hotels and lasts roughly 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Old Port waterfront as the sun sets, then head to Just for Laughs Festival Street Performances (festival runs mid-July). Catch free outdoor comedy acts, street artists, and live entertainment at Place des Arts or St-Denis Street — a perfect low-key introduction to Montreal's festival scene.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick bite at the airport upon landing.
meals.lunch: Snacks and tastings included in the Old Montreal Culinary Walking Tour (charcuterie, local cheese, fresh bread).
meals.dinner: Olive + Gourmando (Old Montreal) — a beloved local bistro known for creative sandwiches, seasonal plates, and Quebec-sourced ingredients. Mid-range pricing (~$25–$40 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: July is peak Just for Laughs season — check the official festival schedule at hahaha.com for free outdoor show times. Wear comfortable walking shoes for cobblestone streets. Keep luggage light on arrival day.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take the metro (Orange Line, Jean-Talon station) to one of North America's largest open-air markets. Sample Quebec cheeses, maple taffy, fresh fruit, artisan charcuterie, and local pastries with a guided tour group. Arrive early (~9:30 AM) for the best produce and smallest crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood on foot. Browse indie boutiques and murals on Avenue du Mont-Royal, then rent a BIXI bike (~$7/30 min) to ride up to Parc du Mont-Royal for panoramic city views. Enjoy the warm summer weather with a relaxed picnic on the mountain using market finds from the morning.
day_by_day.evening: St-Laurent Boulevard Street Food & Nightlife Crawl: Head to 'The Main' as evening energy picks up. Walk from Sherbrooke to Laurier sampling smoked meat sandwiches at Schwartz's Deli, Portuguese chicken at Rotisserie Romados, and end with a craft beer at a local bar like Brasserie Harricana.

meals.breakfast: Café Olimpico (Mile End) — iconic Montreal café with espresso and buttery croissants; a neighbourhood institution (~$10–$15 CAD).
meals.lunch: Picnic assembled from Jean-Talon Market: local cheeses, cured meats, fresh baguette, seasonal fruit, and maple treats (~$20 CAD self-curated).
meals.dinner: Schwartz's Hebrew Delicatessen on St-Laurent — the legendary smoked meat sandwich with coleslaw and a cherry Coke is a Montreal rite of passage (~$20–$30 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is busiest on weekend mornings — a Thursday visit is a sweet spot. Bring cash for market vendors. BIXI bike helmets are available at rental stations. St-Laurent crawl works best starting around 6:30–7:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience (summer edition events): Check the festival program for daytime gastronomy workshops, chef demonstrations, or pop-up tastings happening around the city. Alternatively, explore the Atwater Market in the Sud-Ouest neighbourhood for a quieter, more local market experience with artisan producers and a riverside setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Montréal (Montreal Museum of Fine Arts) for a cultural afternoon. The permanent collection is free; special exhibitions are ~$24 CAD. Afterward, wander through the Golden Square Mile and Sherbrooke Street boutiques. Stop for a gelato or pastry at a café on Bishop or Crescent Street.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Evening Shows: Return to the festival zone for headline free outdoor performances. If budget allows, consider purchasing a ticket (~$40–$80 CAD) for an indoor comedy gala at Théâtre St-Denis — book in advance online. Cap the night with a drink at a rooftop bar in the Quartier des Spectacles.

meals.breakfast: Arthurs Nosh Bar (Notre-Dame-de-Grâce) or a local café near the hotel — try a Montreal-style bagel with smoked salmon and cream cheese (~$12–$18 CAD).
meals.lunch: Lemeac Café Bistro (Outremont) — classic French-Quebec bistro fare; the two-course lunch special is excellent value (~$25–$35 CAD).
meals.dinner: Joe Beef or Liverpool House (Little Burgundy) — iconic Montreal restaurants celebrating local ingredients and Quebec terroir. Reservations strongly recommended. Budget ~$60–$90 CAD per person for a full experience.

day_by_day.notes: Friday evenings at Just for Laughs are especially lively — arrive at outdoor venues 30 minutes early for a good spot. Joe Beef reservations should be made weeks in advance; Liverpool House is slightly easier to book. Check festival.montreal.com for updated event listings.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning in Old Montreal: Visit the Notre-Dame Basilica (AURA light show tickets available for evening, but daytime entry is ~$15 CAD). Explore the Marché Bonsecours and browse local artisan crafts. Walk along the Old Port and rent a pedal boat or kayak on the St. Lawrence River for a fun outdoor activity in the warm summer weather.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Plateau or Mile End for a final neighbourhood wander. Visit a local record shop or bookstore on Saint-Denis Street. Head to Parc Lafontaine for a relaxing afternoon among locals — bring a book, watch street musicians, or simply soak in the quintessential Montreal summer atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Old Montreal, close to the hotel. Explore the festival zone one last time for any remaining Just for Laughs street performances or wrap-up events. Pick up local souvenirs — Quebec maple syrup, local craft beer, or artisan chocolate — from shops near the hotel before calling it a night.

meals.breakfast: Le Cartet (Old Montreal) — beloved neighbourhood spot for weekend brunch with freshly baked goods, eggs, and strong coffee (~$18–$28 CAD).
meals.lunch: Fairmount Bagel or St-Viateur Bagel (Mile End) — grab a dozen freshly baked Montreal bagels with toppings for a casual, iconic lunch (~$10–$15 CAD).
meals.dinner: Holder Restaurant (Old Montreal) — elegant but approachable French brasserie with Quebec-inspired dishes and a great wine list; perfect for a celebratory last dinner (~$45–$65 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Saturday markets and festivals are at peak energy — expect crowds but also the best atmosphere. If departing on July 19, confirm hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late flight. Montreal's metro and buses run frequently on weekends. Consider buying local maple products as gifts — Jean-Talon and Atwater markets have the best selection and prices.

Interact with passionate vendors and learn about Quebec's rich agricultural traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood at your own pace — browse independent boutiques and galleries along Avenue Laurier, visit the beautiful Parc La Fontaine, and soak in the vibrant local culture. Consider a visit to the Musée des beaux-arts de Montréal (Montreal Museum of Fine Arts) for world-class art in a stunning building.

Cap the night at a sophisticated cocktail lounge on the boulevard.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or at Crew Collective & Café, a stunning café inside a former Royal Bank hall near Old Montreal — enjoy freshly baked croissants, seasonal fruit, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: At Jean-Talon Market, assemble a gourmet picnic from market vendors — aged cheddar, duck rillettes, fresh baguette, heirloom tomatoes, and a bottle of Quebec cider. Enjoy at a market-side table.
meals.dinner: Joe Beef — one of Canada's most celebrated restaurants on Rue Notre-Dame Ouest. Known for its decadent, ingredient-driven menu featuring oysters, foie gras, and exceptional steak, paired with a legendary wine list. A true Montreal institution.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is most vibrant in the morning — aim to arrive by 9:00–9:30 AM. Book a private or small-group premium food tour through a reputable local operator. Joe Beef is extremely popular — reservations are essential and should be made weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience (summer edition): Attend the gastronomy and performing arts programming associated with this premier Montreal festival. Explore curated chef collaborations, artisan food pavilions, and immersive culinary demonstrations hosted at various premium venues across the city. Check the 2027 festival program for morning pop-up events and exclusive tastings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Mont Royal Park for a scenic afternoon — hike or take a horse-drawn calèche to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for panoramic views of the Montreal skyline and the St. Lawrence River. Afterward, explore the charming Mile End neighbourhood, known for its creative energy, world-famous bagel bakeries (St-Viateur Bagel), and independent coffee culture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Just for Laughs Festival for a premium ticketed indoor show at one of the festival's headline venues — world-class comedians perform in intimate theatres across the city. Pre-show, enjoy cocktails at a chic Old Montreal bar. Post-show, explore the lively festival atmosphere with live music and outdoor performances.

meals.breakfast: Le Cartet in Old Montreal — a beloved brunch destination offering beautifully prepared eggs Benedict, smoked salmon platters, fresh pastries, and excellent coffee in a warm, market-style setting.
meals.lunch: St-Viateur Bagel & Café in Mile End — enjoy the world-renowned Montreal-style wood-fired bagels with premium smoked salmon, cream cheese, capers, and red onion. A quintessential Montreal experience.
meals.dinner: Le Mousso — a cutting-edge tasting menu restaurant by celebrated chef Antonin Monat. Offers a bold, creative multi-course experience with locally sourced ingredients and innovative technique. One of Montreal's most exciting fine-dining destinations.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Just for Laughs premium indoor show tickets well in advance through the official festival website. The Mont Royal hike is approximately 45 minutes each way — wear comfortable shoes. The festival's gastronomy programming may require advance registration for exclusive chef dinners.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Old Montreal — take a private guided architectural walking tour of Vieux-Montréal's historic landmarks, including the Pointe-à-Callière Museum (archaeology and history), the Old Port waterfront promenade, and the magnificent Notre-Dame Basilica interior (book a premium guided visit). Soak in the charm of the cobblestone laneways and 18th-century stone buildings at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a premium spa experience at a luxury hotel spa or the renowned Bota Bota Spa-sur-l'eau — a unique floating spa moored in the Old Port, offering Nordic thermal baths, massage treatments, and stunning river views. A perfect way to rejuvenate before departure. Alternatively, browse the boutiques and galleries of Old Montreal for artisan souvenirs and Quebec-made gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Final farewell dinner in Old Montreal, celebrating the end of a spectacular Montreal journey. Afterward, a private car transfer to the hotel for rest or onward travel arrangements.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel's restaurant or at Olive & Gourmando — enjoy a final indulgent spread of fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, smoked salmon, and expertly brewed coffee while watching Old Montreal come to life on a Saturday morning.
meals.lunch: Garde Manger — Chef Chuck Hughes's beloved Old Montreal seafood-focused bistro. Enjoy a luxurious weekend lunch featuring fresh oysters, lobster, and Quebec seafood in a warm, candlelit setting.
meals.dinner: Maison Boulud at the Ritz-Carlton Montreal — an elegant dining room by world-renowned Chef Daniel Boulud. The menu celebrates French culinary tradition with Quebec ingredients, complemented by an exceptional wine cellar and impeccable service. The perfect grand finale to a luxury Montreal trip.

day_by_day.notes: Book Bota Bota spa treatments in advance, especially for a Saturday. Notre-Dame Basilica interior visits may require timed entry tickets — reserve online. Confirm hotel checkout time and arrange a private luxury transfer to the airport or onward destination in advance through your concierge.
